The author of the 'Harry Potter' series is J.K. Rowling.

The space station, a relic of a forgotten era, orbited the desolate planet known as Xylos Prime. Historically, Xylos Prime was once a thriving agricultural hub during the Galactic Expansion of the 24th century, but its collapse was precipitated by the Great Silica Blight, a nanite-based plague that consumed all organic matter and left the surface barren and gray. The station itself, named *The Aegis*, was constructed as a mining outpost to harvest the rare isotopes found in the planet’s crust, but it was abandoned after the blight mutated, rendering the automated systems hostile to human life.

Now, the station drifts in silent orbit, its metallic corridors echoing with the solitary hum of machinery that has long since lost its purpose. The air inside is stale, recycled through filters that are slowly failing, carrying the faint scent of ozone and old dust. Outside the viewing ports, a ballet of asteroids dances against the inky backdrop of space, remnants of the planet’s shattered moon, which was destroyed in the initial stages of the blight’s spread. These asteroids, varying in size from pebbles to small moons, reflect the dim light of the distant sun, creating a hauntingly beautiful spectacle that contrasts sharply with the desolation below. The station’s AI, now degraded and fragmented, occasionally broadcasts fragmented logs of the past, whispering stories of a time when Xylos Prime was green and alive, serving as a ghostly reminder of what was lost.
